prompt_md: A disease affects 1 in 1,000 people. A test for it is 99% accurate. You test positive. What's the chance you actually have the disease?
prompt_short: A 99% accurate test, a 1-in-1,000 disease. You test positive. Chance you have it?
hint_md: Imagine testing 1,000 people. How many positives are real?
explain_intuition_md: Test 1,000 people. About 1 is sick and tests positive. About 10 healthy people also test positive by mistake. So only about 1 in 11 positives is real.
explain_math_md:
$$P(\text{sick} \mid +) = \frac{0.99 \times 0.001}{0.99 \times 0.001 + 0.01 \times 0.999} \approx 0.0902$$

"99% accurate" means both a 99% true-positive rate and a 99% true-negative rate.
